purpose: Fenoprofen is used to relieve pain, swelling, and stiffness caused by arthritis, including rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis. It can also be used for mild to moderate pain from other causes. It helps you move more comfortably and feel better day to day.
how_it_works: Your body makes certain chemicals called prostaglandins that cause pain, swelling, and fever. Fenoprofen works by blocking the enzymes that produce these chemicals, so less of them are made. With fewer of these chemicals around, you experience less pain and inflammation.
common_side_effects: Upset stomach, nausea, heartburn, or indigestion are the most common complaints. Some people also notice headache, dizziness, drowsiness, or constipation. Taking the medication with food or milk can help reduce stomach upset.
warnings: This medication can increase the risk of serious stomach bleeding or ulcers, especially if you take it for a long time or at high doses. It may also raise your risk of heart attack or stroke, so it should be used with caution if you have heart disease. Avoid using it if you are pregnant, especially in the last 3 months. Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, as this drug can affect those organs. Do not take it with other NSAIDs like ibuprofen or naproxen.
typical_dosing: For arthritis, the usual dose is 300 to 600 mg taken 3 to 4 times a day, with a maximum of 3,200 mg per day. For general pain relief, 200 mg every 4 to 6 hours as needed is typical. Always take the lowest dose that works for you, and follow your doctor's specific instructions.
